clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed on January 9, 2025, as a mark of respect for James Earl 
Carter, Jr., the thirty-ninth President of the United States.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
January 9, 2025, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public 
need.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. January 9, 2025, shall be considered as falling within the scope 
of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 
6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and 
leave of employees of the United States.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text:
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order.

clauses.label: Sec. 5.
clauses.text:
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect:

clauses.label: (i)
clauses.text:
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or

clauses.label: (ii)
clauses.text:
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations.

own_original_text:
Executive Order 14133 of December 30, 2024 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on January 9, 2025 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed on January 9, 2025, as a mark of respect for James Earl 
Carter, Jr., the thirty-ninth President of the United States. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
January 9, 2025, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public 
need. 
Sec. 3. January 9, 2025, shall be considered as falling within the scope 
of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 
6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and 
leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 14133, 90 FR 187 (Federal Register Vol. 90, No. 2, Friday, January 3, 2025; filed January 2, 2025), signed December 30, 2024 (grade official_original_counted, machine text layer of the official PDF). The heading, number, title (Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on January 9, 2025) and date agree with the census register. Text and inventory: I read the whole held text. It has sections 1 to 5 (section 5 with its sub-items), with no separate lead clause; the dossier's clause inventory matches those paragraphs and is complete. Lifecycle: the order closes the departments and agencies on January 9, 2025 and says nothing that runs past January 9, 2025, so every clause ends by the order's own terms on 2025-01-09 (section 5(d) excepted where it is dated separately). No later instrument names the order: the packet's lookup of held order texts for its number lists only its own Federal Register text, and the dossier's later-event chain is empty. The only other instrument the text names is Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, an earlier order cited in section 3.
